properties.name: diagram-assistant
properties.purpose: An agent loop whose one tool is an MCP server's: the catalog row render_diagram maps to the route diagram.render, which the MCP binding of a language pack serves by calling a Mermaid MCP server over streamable HTTP. The graph names a route, the binding names the server, and the engine stays MCP-free (RFC-0011 / ADR-0033 step 4)
The knowledge layer: the tool catalog and the error handler

The catalog: one row, written on the graph after reviewing the server's own description with the binding's describe command. The model reads this text, never the server's; the input schema is the loop's closed subset, so the server's $schema keyword stays out
A run needs the description of the diagram before any token is spent

mapping: text(Missing question. Describe the diagram in the 'question' field) -> output.body.message
properties.purpose: Reject a request without a description

input: text(You are a diagram assistant for software teams. Turn the user's description into one Mermaid diagram. Always validate it with the render_diagram tool before you answer. If the tool reports the diagram invalid, fix the code and validate again. Answer with the validated Mermaid code in a fenced mermaid block, then one sentence on what the diagram shows. Never answer with a diagram the tool has not validated.) -> system
properties.purpose: The agent loop: the model drafts the Mermaid code, the loop calls diagram.render through the binding, and the model answers with the validated code or fixes it and tries again. result_limit cuts the tool's reply at 8 KiB: the server returns the rendered image too, and the model needs the verdict and the code, not the image
The graph decides on the loop's status
The validated diagram, with the call log and the usage

mapping: text(The model stopped without an answer. The status says why) -> output.body.message

properties.purpose: The loop's own failure: a bad catalog, llm.chat unreachable or failing
